title: Security Analyst Roadmap
summary: Build a strong foundation in networking, Linux, security operations, detection, incident response and cloud security, then use projects and internships to move into security-operations or security-engineering roles.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a four-year B.Tech/B.E. programme beginning in 2026 and graduating around 2030. If your programme or graduation year differs, shift the timeline accordingly.

about.label: Career-route check
about.text: Security Analyst is a direct career path for CSE - Cyber Security.

blocks.text: Build a strong foundation in networking, Linux, security operations, detection, incident response and cloud security, then use projects and internships to move into security-operations or security-engineering roles.

blocks.text: 4-year honours variant

If your university offers the four-year honours route, use the additional year for deeper research, advanced security engineering, a substantial dissertation/project, industry work or preparation for postgraduate study. Do not assume the honours year is required for an entry-level Security Analyst position.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Move beyond alert handling into detection engineering, cloud security, security architecture, threat-informed defence, automation and security leadership. Keep a working knowledge of AI-assisted security operations while retaining the ability to validate alerts and findings independently.

blocks.label: Visa and job-offer note
blocks.text: A university admission, student visa, post-study work permission and eventual job offer are separate processes. Verify the immigration rules for the year you apply.
Typical timing is approximately 0–2 years → 2–5 years → 5–8 years → 8–12 years → 12+ years, but actual progression depends on role, employer, technical depth and leadership responsibilities.
PhD routes

At senior levels, maintain relevance by combining deep technical expertise with architecture, risk management, security strategy, automation and mentoring. A Security Analyst who progresses into senior technical or management work should continue to understand the underlying evidence behind security decisions rather than relying entirely on automated tooling.
